objective: Specify and exercise the existing continuous byte-stream adaptation: WebSocket message boundaries do not define RPC messages.

source_decision.transport: The existing native admission handle transfers an accepted WebSocket into the existing TunnelStream. HTTP/2 reads and writes the ordered bytes as one continuous stream across arbitrary binary WebSocket message boundaries.
refusals: NativeAdmission reports Full when the bounded pending-connection reservation is exhausted.
NativeAdmission reports Closed after its NativeIncoming receiver is dropped.
The existing adapter visibly rejects unsupported messages, oversize input, and truncated HTTP/2 input.
source_decision.ownership: The accepted connection owns the WebSocket pump and both byte directions; dropping either end terminates the pump and releases pipe owners.

new_public_boundary_test.name: websocket_messages_are_only_chunks_of_the_http2_byte_stream
new_public_boundary_test.procedure: Start an owned loopback Axum WebSocket endpoint using NativeAdmission and NativeIncoming; pass the admitted public TunnelStream to an actual h2 server handshake; run an h2 client over the direct seven-byte test adapter or a bounded DuplexStream with an independently owned WebSocket pump; echo a request body through the real native adapter.
delivery_shapes: The split mode sends each AsyncWrite portion as a distinct binary WebSocket message, caps each at seven bytes, reconstructs the observed wire bytes, and checks the actual HTTP/2 preface is preserved.

The coalescing mode writes actual h2 bytes into a bounded 64 KiB DuplexStream, whose flush completes to its peer byte pipe. An independently owned pump then groups the request bytes after the server handshake until the last body marker and sends them as one binary WebSocket message.

The coalescing assertion requires both separated body markers, more than FRAME_BYTES apart, to appear in one observed WebSocket message. Since one HTTP/2 DATA frame carries at most FRAME_BYTES payload bytes, this proves at least two DATA frames shared that message without parsing or reimplementing HTTP/2 framing.
Run a real HTTP/2 request/response through the tunnel and compare the exact echoed 32 KiB body.
new_public_boundary_test.cleanup: Observe public ConnectionMetrics after the WebSocket pumps complete; require closed connection state and zero pipe owners. The coalescing client pump is joined or cancelled and reaped within a finite bound. A late inbound BrokenPipe is terminal only after the exact response and actual coalescence assertions complete and the owned h2 driver returns Ok; earlier or other pipe failures remain assertions.

coalescence_evidence.method: Record exact outbound binary WebSocket messages from the h2 client's AsyncWrite adapter.
coalescence_evidence.required_assertion: A single recorded message contains the first and last unique body markers separated by more than FRAME_BYTES.
coalescence_evidence.frame_parsing: None; the test relies on the established HTTP/2 maximum DATA payload size and the actual payload markers.

new_typed_admission_test.name: native_admission_reports_full_and_closed_as_typed_refusals
cases: The second reservation against a capacity-one pending queue returns AdmissionError::Full.
Dropping a reservation releases its slot.
Dropping NativeIncoming makes subsequent reservations return AdmissionError::Closed.

alternatives.choice: Keep the existing binary WebSocket-to-TunnelStream adapter and test its public admission/stream boundary.
alternatives.reason: This preserves the existing HTTP/2 and tonic wire protocol and current resource owner.

alternatives.rejected: Interpret each WebSocket message as one RPC request or HTTP/2 frame.
alternatives.reason: WebSocket messages are arbitrary transport chunks; the existing RPC stack requires an ordered continuous byte stream.

alternatives.reason: Those changes exceed the frozen two-file scope and duplicate or bypass the existing adapter.
